content.thinking:
I'm planning to write the file carefully in one pass, sticking to familiar API patterns. I'm sketching out the swamp troll's design: a hunched, chunky Warcraft-style creature around 2.6m tall with oversized hands and shoulders, a small head, tusked jaw, mottled green-teal skin, hide loincloth, spiked club, moss and mushrooms, bark pauldron, rope belt, and skull trophies.

I'm working out specific coordinates for the troll's hunched pose—hips, belly, chest, shoulders, head, and long dangling arms—to hit roughly 2.6m total height, then thinking through the paint layers using mottled and countershaded skin tones for a hand-painted Warcraft look.

Writing leg geometry...

Still placing hand, finger, and head anatomy...

Positioning the belt torus against the belly curve, accepting slight clipping since it's minor. Now sketching the loincloth as an extruded flap hanging at the front.

Still writing club geometry...

For warts I'm scattering small spheres across the belly surface using a randomized distribution with minimum spacing, sticking them onto the body frame. For markings I'm layering a countershading paint between the back mottle and lighter belly tone.

Still writing material and geometry helpers...

Working out teeth placement with small ivory cones along the jaw arc, then computing eye and brow positions on the skull sphere using geometric projections so they sit properly embedded into the surface.

The brow sloping from inner to outer edges looks right, and keeping the head angled forward works too. The neck should be hidden under the shoulders, so I'll finalize this layout.
